To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the finite element analyses using the MCC and HS are validated by comparing the centrifugal tests, and further extended to propose two new alternative analytical models to describe the three-dimensional failure envelope of the suction bucket foundation under vertical, horizontal and moment loads in clay.
the proposed macro element design models based on the two constitutive models are applicable to predict the behaviour of suction bucket foundation with high efficiency.
the finite element simulations are reliable and the macro element design models are efficient and accurate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modelling of suction bucket foundation from full finite element simulations to macro element models.
the modelling of the suction bucket foundation under both monotonic and cycling conditions.
the modelling of the suction bucket foundation under both monotonic and cycling loading conditions in clay from finite element analyses to the macro element.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the finite element analyses of suction bucket foundation are very useful and reliable for the understanding of the mechanism and the failure pattern of foundation in clay.

, the proposed two new alternative analytical and macro element models are both applicable to describe the 3D failure envelope of suction bucket foundation and the proposed macro element design model based on the HS model is slightly more accurate than that based on the MCC model.

the finite element analysis using HS model is the most accurate method to predict the failure patterns and the failure envelope in V HM space, while the new alternative macro element model using HS model is a good alternative for practical design of suction bucket foundation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite element analyses using MCC and HS models are reliable and the proposed analytical formulations are accurate and the macro element model based on HS has better performance.

the finite element analyses using MCC and HS models can be used to predict the failure patterns of suction bucket foundations in clay and the proposed macro element design models can be used as an alternative to predict the ultimate bearing capacity of suction bucket foundations for both monotonic loading and cyclic loading conditions.
the finite element analyses are very reliable and can provide valuable information to understand the behaviour of the suction bucket foundation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the finite element analyses using MCC and HS are able to provide accurate and reliable results and both models are able to describe the failure envelope in V HM space.
both MCC and HS are able to describe the behaviour of the foundation soil and the foundation system reasonably well.

the proposed macro element design models based on both MCC and HS can predict the failure envelope of suction bucket foundation under cyclic loading conditions and the results can be used to design the suction bucket foundation.
